rationales: Smoke consists of solid particles dispersed in air, a gas.
Butter is a solid-in-solid colloid, not a solid-in-gas solution.
Brass is a solid solution of metals, not a solid-in-gas solution.
Fog consists of liquid droplets dispersed in air.
Carbon belongs to group 14, not group 15.
Sulphur belongs to group 16.
Nitrogen is a non-metal in group 15.
Iodine belongs to group 17.
Dobereiner proposed the law of triads.
Newlands presented the law of octaves.
Moseley arranged elements by atomic number.
Mendeleev proposed the periodic law and periodic table.
An ionic bond forms through electron transfer and electrostatic attraction.
A covalent bond forms through mutual sharing of electrons.
A metallic bond involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
A coordinate bond forms when one atom supplies both shared electrons.
800 °C is far below sodium chloride’s boiling point.
1013 °C is below sodium chloride’s boiling point.
1213 °C is below sodium chloride’s boiling point.
The listed textbook value for sodium chloride’s boiling point is 1413 °C.
Zinc is solid at room temperature.
Sodium is solid at room temperature.
Hydrogen is a gas at room temperature.
Mercury is liquid at room temperature.
% m/m expresses mass of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% m/v expresses grams of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
% v/m expresses cm³ of solute per 100 grams of solution.
% v/v expresses cm³ of solute per 100 cm³ of solution.
377 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
403 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
419 kJ/mol is not sodium’s first ionization energy.
Sodium’s first ionization energy is approximately 496 kJ/mol.
Thomson proposed the plum pudding model of the atom.
Chadwick discovered the neutron.
Goldstein observed canal rays.
Dalton proposed an early solid-sphere atomic model.
600 °C is below sodium chloride’s melting point.
750 °C is below sodium chloride’s melting point.
Sodium chloride melts at about 801 °C, conventionally given as 800 °C.
1000 °C is above sodium chloride’s melting point.
Solvent-to-solute is the inverse of the usual concentration ratio.
Concentration is commonly expressed as the amount of solute relative to the solution.
Solvent-to-solution describes the solvent fraction, not solute concentration.
Solute-to-solvent is not the usual ratio defining concentration.
Calcium is heavier than lithium.
Magnesium is heavier than lithium.
Lithium is the lightest metal.
Sodium is heavier than lithium.
H. Moseley established atomic number as the basis for arranging elements.
Newlands proposed the law of octaves.
Thomson discovered the electron.
Crookes studied cathode rays but did not discover atomic number.
HCl is polar because its atoms have unequal electronegativity.
NH₃ is polar due to its trigonal-pyramidal shape.
H₂O is polar due to its bent shape.
H₂ is non-polar because its identical atoms share electrons equally.
Zinc is used to galvanize iron and steel.
Chromium is commonly used for plating, not galvanizing.
Copper is not the metal used to galvanize iron and steel.
Iron is the metal commonly protected by galvanizing, not the coating metal.
